subject: Private VPC: control-plane affinity, data-plane egress ledger & runbook
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Stuart Hayes <stuart.hayes@stellara.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private VPC: control-plane affinity, data-plane egress ledger & runbook

Stuart —

Thanks for agreeing to a short architecture readout on the private VPC handoff. Attached is the current diagram and a first-pass runbook for this deployment. Two items we want to lock in during this thread so the deploy runbook can be finalized:

1) Control-plane affinity: can we confirm which rack-level or VLAN-level endpoints the Stellara colo team will allow control-plane traffic from? We need an explicit set of IPs/subnets so our control-plane can be pinned to dedicated management interfaces (we prefer non-overlapping subnets to simplify KMS/KV cache isolation).

2) Data-plane egress ledger: the customer requires a strict audit of egress NATs and a deterministic mapping so security can map tenant traffic to audit IPs. Can you confirm whether egress NATs will be done at the fabric edge (ASN/BGP NAT) or inside the tenant overlay (NAT gateway)? Also any constraints on static source IPs for outbound 3rd-party integrations?

Attached: segregation-diagram-v3.png (image/png), runbook-draft-v1.md (text/markdown)

Proposed next steps: a quick 30-min call tomorrow to confirm the IP lists and where we should put the ephemeral NATs. If you prefer to reply here with the specifics that works fine too.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: segregation-diagram-v3.png]
[Attachment: runbook-draft-v1.md]

From: Stuart Hayes <stuart.hayes@stellara.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@stellara.com
Date: 2028-04-20T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: control-plane affinity, data-plane egress ledger & runbook

Rachel —

Appreciate the clear ask. Answers below, and I attached our egress policy PDF for the audit team.

On 2028-04-20 at 08:12, Rachel Kim wrote:
> Stuart —
>
> Thanks for agreeing to a short architecture readout on the private VPC handoff...

1) Control-plane affinity:
- Our colo ops will accept control-plane management interfaces from the management VLAN only (10.240.200.0/24). We will also reserve two /29 blocks for vendor control-plane peering: 10.240.201.0/29 and 10.240.201.8/29. These are routable across the site fabric and can be announced to your peering.

2) Data-plane egress ledger:
- Egress NAT is performed at the fabric edge today. We can provide static SNAT pools mapped to tenant tags. The default is a pool per-tenant (public IPs x.x.57.0/28 mapped to tenant-id).
- If you need per-subnet static IPs we can do that but it will require an additional allocation and a config change in our BGP announcement plan.

Constraints:
- Outbound TLS inspection is enabled by default for managed tenants; if your deployment requires bypass for certain destinations we need the destination CIDRs & FQDNs up front.
- Time to request additional static IP allocation is ~72 hours (procurement + ASN announce).

I've attached the Stellara egress policy PDF (stellara-egress-policy.pdf) with audit mappings and contact points. Happy to jump on a call — I can do 09:30 PT tomorrow.

Stuart Hayes
Senior Network Architect
Stellara Cloud
[Attachment: stellara-egress-policy.pdf]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stuart Hayes <stuart.hayes@stellara.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-04-20T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: control-plane affinity, data-plane egress ledger & runbook

Quick clarifications from our infra side —

> On 2028-04-20, Stuart Hayes wrote:
> > 1) Control-plane affinity: our colo ops will accept control-plane management interfaces from the management VLAN only (10.240.200.0/24)...

We can pin our control-plane to the two /29 blocks Stuart listed (10.240.201.0/29 and .8/29). That gives us room for:
- Primary control-plane cluster (2 management IPs)
- Secondary (standby) control-plane cluster (2 IPs)
- Day-2 ops & KMS reachability (1 IP)

Technical asks from our side:
- We need an L3 reachability test window pre-cutover to verify KMS TLS validation and control-plane handshake (we will provide test certs).
- For data-plane egress: we prefer fabric-edge NAT (Stellara's default) — simplifies our KV cache mapping. We'll populate a mapping file that associates tenant-id -> public IPs and send to ops@stellara.com.

Operational notes:
- If egress is performed at fabric edge, ensure the SNAT mapping file is versioned and stored in the runbook (SUP-4237 will track).
- Canary behavior: if NAT pool is exhausted we will fallback to a smaller burst pool; we need explicit owner for burst pool notifications (suggest: ops@stellara.com).

I'll open the Jira ticket and link the mapping file to the runbook.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stuart Hayes <stuart.hayes@stellara.com>, ops@stellara.com
Date: 2028-04-21T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: control-plane affinity, data-plane egress ledger & runbook

Thanks — this is great, team. Summary / decisions and action owners: 

Decisions:
- Control-plane affinity: Redwood will use the two /29 blocks (10.240.201.0/29 and 10.240.201.8/29) for control-plane endpoints.
- Data-plane egress: use fabric-edge SNAT pools mapped per-tenant (Stellara to provide initial pool x.x.57.0/28).
- TLS inspection: default enabled; Redwood will submit allowlist FQDNs for bypass where required.

Action items:
- Stuart / Stellara ops: provide the confirmed SNAT pool allocation and the contact for burst-pool notifications by 2028-04-23. (owner: ops@stellara.com)
- Karthik: open Jira SUP-4237, attach the runbook-draft-v1.md and add the tenant-id -> public IP mapping template. (owner: karthik_iyer, due: 2028-04-22)
- Kimberly: finalize the runbook section describing the L3 reachability test and include cert exchange steps. (owner: kimberly_park, due: 2028-04-22)
- Rachel: update the Drive design folder with final diagram and version the runbook. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_CD-PrivateVPC-Design (owner: rachel_kim, due: 2028-04-24)

I've attached a cleaned export of the diagram and the current runbook draft for your records. If anyone needs a quick sync I'll schedule a 30-min call for 09:30 PT tomorrow per Stuart's availability.

Thanks all —
Rachel Kim
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
